---
title: "2026 Florida Republican Primary for Governor"
format: html
execute:
  echo: false
  message: false
  warning: false
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(sf)
library(tigris)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# Extract county precinct files to a temporary directory and read them all at once
tmp_dir <- tempdir()
files <- unzip("2026-pri-outputofficial.zip", exdir = tmp_dir)

gov_rep_raw <- read_tsv(
  files,
  col_names = FALSE,
  col_select = c(
    county = X2,
    office = X12,
    candidate = X15,
    party = X16,
    votes = X19
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(office == "Governor", party == "REP")

county_winners <- gov_rep_raw |>
  summarize(votes = sum(votes, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(county, candidate)) |>
  mutate(
    vote_share = votes / sum(votes),
    county_key = str_to_lower(county),
    .by = county
  ) |>
  slice_max(votes, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = county)

fl_counties <- counties(state = "FL", cb = TRUE, progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  mutate(county_key = str_to_lower(NAME)) |>
  left_join(county_winners, by = "county_key")

ggplot(fl_counties) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = candidate, alpha = vote_share), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "Winning Candidate") +
  scale_alpha_continuous(
    name = "Vote Share",
    labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1),
    range = c(0.4, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Winning Candidate by County: 2026 Republican Primary for Governor",
    subtitle = "Shaded by the winner's share of the county vote",
    caption = "Source: Florida Department of State & U.S. Census Bureau (tigris)"
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

## Candidate Benefits & Key Proposals

- **Byron Donalds** (won 50 counties): Promised a business-friendly, low-tax economy, further deregulation to ease inflation costs, and expanded school choice paired with workforce-ready education pathways.
- **Jay Collins** (won 17 counties): Emphasized continuity with the DeSantis administration, enhanced support for law enforcement, military families, and veterans, and stronger state infrastructure and disaster resiliency.
- **James Fishback**: Campaigned on eliminating property taxes, rolling local government spending back to 2021 levels to lower the cost of living, and protecting local power grids and water resources from large data centers.
- **Paul Renner**: Highlighted his legislative record on universal school choice and fiscal restraint, proposing further cuts to state red tape and relief from high property insurance rates for Florida homeowners.
